cards.title: Where JavaScript fits — bringing webpages to life!
cards.takeaway: HTML builds the page content, CSS styles how it looks, and JavaScript adds brains — calculations, clicks, carts, and live updates.
cards.body:
You already know a static webpage shows words and pictures. **JavaScript (JS)** is what turns a poster into a **working app**!

- **HTML:** Structure (headings, buttons, inputs).
- **CSS:** Look and layout (colours, fonts, spacing).
- **JavaScript:** Action & logic (calculating a 5% shop discount, updating a cart total, validating a form).

cards.title: Linking `js/app.js` at the bottom of `<body>`
cards.takeaway: Write `<script src="js/app.js"></script>` right before `</body>` so all HTML elements load BEFORE JavaScript tries to use them!
cards.body:
Keep your JavaScript in its own clean file (like `js/app.js`) and connect it right before the closing `</body>` tag:

```html
  <script src="js/app.js"></script>
</body>
```

**Why at the bottom of `<body>` instead of inside `<head>`?**
Because browsers read top-to-bottom! Putting `<script>` at the bottom lets your visible HTML load first so the screen feels fast and every button/heading already exists when your JS runs.

check.prompt: Which line properly links an external file at `js/app.js`, and where in `index.html` do we usually place it?

choices.text: `<script src="js/app.js"></script>` right before the closing `</body>` tag
`<link href="js/app.js">` at the very top before `<html>`

check.hint: External JS uses `<script src="..."></script>` after the page's HTML content.
check.explanation: Spot on! `<script src="js/app.js"></script>` right before `</body>` ensures your HTML elements exist before the script runs.

cards.title: Variables (`const` & `let`) and the DevTools Console
cards.takeaway: A variable is a labelled box storing a value (`const` if it stays fixed, `let` if it changes), and `console.log()` prints to DevTools.
cards.body:
Think of a **variable** as a neat storage box with a name sticker on the front:
- **`const`** — for values that **won't be reassigned** (`const vatRate = 0.075;`)
- **`let`** — for values that **change later** (`let cartTotal = 0;`)

Press **`F12`** (or right-click → **Inspect → Console**) in Chrome to open the **Console** — your X-ray window where `console.log(cartTotal)` prints values and shows helpful error line numbers!

cards.title: The 4 core JavaScript data types
cards.takeaway: `string` = text in quotes, `number` = plain digits for math, `boolean` = `true`/`false`, and `undefined` = declared box with no value yet.
cards.body:
JavaScript treats values according to their **type**:
- **`string`:** Text wrapped in quotes — `"Port Harcourt"` or `'₦7,500'`.
- **`number`:** Raw digits with **no quotes and no commas** — `7500` or `0.05`.
- **`boolean`:** Yes/No switch — `true` or `false` (no quotes!).
- **`undefined`:** A variable created with `let x;` before anything is put inside.

check.prompt: What happens if you write `let price = "two thousand"; console.log(price * 2);`?

choices.text: It produces `NaN` (Not a Number) because you cannot multiply words — store `2000` as a number without quotes!

check.hint: Math (`*`, `-`, `/`) needs a real numeric value like `2000`, not English words in quotes!
check.explanation: Exactly! Multiplying non-numeric text gives `NaN`. Keep prices as plain numbers (`let price = 2000;`) so math works cleanly.

cards.title: Real shop math: calculating a 5% discount in 2 lines
cards.takeaway: Multiply price by `0.05` for the discount, then subtract it from price to get the final amount to pay.
cards.body:
Suppose a Lagos shop sells a bag for **₦7,500** with a **5% (`0.05`)** discount:

```js
const price = 7500;
const discount = price * 0.05;      // 375
const finalPrice = price - discount; // 7125
console.log(finalPrice);
```

Notice there are **no quotes** and **no `₦` or comma** inside `7500` — we add `'₦'` only when displaying the final message to the shopper!

cards.title: Watch out for the `'4500' + 450 = '4500450'` string trap!
cards.takeaway: In JavaScript, `+` glues strings together — `'4500' + 450` becomes `'4500450'`, so convert text inputs with `Number(...)` before adding!
cards.body:
Why did `'4500' + 450` become `'4500450'` instead of `4950`?
Because `'4500'` is in **quotes** (a `string`), so `+` glues the characters end-to-end!

**Easy fix:** Keep money values as real numbers (`4500 + 450` → `4950`) or wrap form text in `Number(inputValue)` before adding.

check.prompt: A bag costs `7500` and has a 5% (`0.05`) discount. Which JavaScript snippet computes the final price accurately?
check.hint: 5% as a decimal is `0.05`, and prices in calculations are plain numbers without symbols.
